topics.topic: Customer facts and fiscal data that survive erasure
questions: When this action succeeds, are kind, tax id, legal name, restriction state and relationship-end date also erased, or does some of that data survive?
Does erasing a customer also erase tax id and legal name, or do those fiscal values remain stored in an erased and otherwise unusable Customer?
Exactly which Customer facts survive erasure, especially fiscal data, kind, restriction state and relationship-end date?

judgement.why: This asks the same question about which customer and fiscal fields survive erasure, and the relevant text has not changed.

precedent.topic: Which customer and fiscal fields survive customer erasure
quotes:
Erasing a customer's contact data (R0-06) is the end of its record: the
Customer keeps its identity and the fact that it was erased, and projects keep
naming it. There is no action that deletes a Customer whole.
precedent.why: Because the erased Customer keeps only its identity and erased fact, kind, tax id and legal name do not survive.

topics.topic: External AI provider trust boundary and permitted Registry-derived disclosures
questions: Does the agent call an external model provider, and if so, which Registry-derived values may be sent to it and under whose trust and retention rules?
Is the model an external system, and what agent inputs and outputs cross that trust boundary?
Is the external AI provider a separate recipient, and which Registry-derived values or disclosure classes may be sent to it through the agent?

quotes: - **Agent** — any language-model agent acting for the owner.

The agent runs in a separate VM Agent on the same
server and reaches the platform only through Kernel's agent channel; Registry's
service API is not reachable from VM Agent.

The rule closes the path by which a `personal_data` value would reach an agent
through Cabinet Kernel and so the agent's AI provider (R0-25, R0-26).

The records of processing, the DPIA screening and, when needed, the DPIA
itself, incident response and the other organisational measures. They are
kept as platform-wide governance — Registry, Cabinet Kernel, Cabinet,
PresuPro, Client Portal and the external AI providers — outside this case,
citing the accepted Workbench decisions.
judgement.divergence: One implementer uses local inference and sends no Registry-derived value outside VM Agent; another sends the agent projection and other agent-visible values to an external model provider, which the owner and external provider notice through disclosure, retention and processing.
judgement.why: The text invokes an agent's AI provider and external AI providers without defining that external system, its trust boundary, or which Registry-derived values cross it.

topics.topic: Revision and concurrency requirements across state-changing owner actions
questions: Which state-changing actions must receive an expected revision, which record revision does each move, and through which read output does the owner obtain the current customer revision?
Exactly which actions require an expected revision, which aggregate's revision they check, and which revisions they advance?
What concurrency token, if any, protects owner changes to session access, pending requests, the one-time import and audit erasure?

Which owner actions must present which revision or access version, and what happens when that version is stale, including nominally idempotent actions such as archiving an archived project or erasing an erased customer?

judgement.why: This repeats the prior question about mutation concurrency preconditions, revision advancement, access versions and stale behavior on the same text.

precedent.topic: Concurrency preconditions and stale-revision behavior for mutations
quotes:
Every change carries CSRF protection and
is validated on the server; a change made against an older revision is refused
(R0-35).

A project, a customer and an object carry a revision that every accepted change
moves. A change states the revision it was made against; a change against an
older revision is refused and nothing changes. Every change is atomic.

Narrowed by R0-45: the object has no revision of its own; a change of it moves
the project's.
the session's granted project ids, its active project if any, whether it has a pending request, and the access version — no `personal_data` value (R0-32, R0-46, R0-64)
precedent.why: Mapping expected versions to mutations, defining version advancement and specifying stale or idempotent behavior are rules and required tests owned by State 2.

topics.topic: Audit-entry coverage for successful, failed, and refused actions
questions: Which successful and refused primary actions produce audit entries, and which are intentionally excluded?
Which exact actions and outcomes create audit entries, and are failed or refused attempts recorded when no state changed?

judgement.why: This repeats the prior question about which accepted, refused and state-changing actions produce audit entries on the same text.

precedent.topic: Which accepted, refused, and state-changing actions produce audit entries
quotes:
Registry records only significant changes of state: changes to projects and
customer records, granting and revoking an agent session's projects,
restricting processing and lifting it, and erasures and anonymisations. Ordinary reads, agent calls and the inner steps of flows
are not recorded in Registry; security events of the infrastructure are
handled by the infrastructure, outside Registry.

- **Audit.** A minimal log of significant changes of state (R0-58): time, the
  acting principal (owner, which service, agent through Kernel), the change,
  the project or customer, the outcome, the contract and release version, and
  a confirmation id where the owner confirmed.
precedent.why: The exact event-selection and outcome-recording criteria are operational rules and required tests owned by State 2.

topics.topic: Compliance handling for imported archived projects named after people
questions: How is an imported archived project whose display name contains a person's name brought into compliance with R0-82?
What happens if the selected import contains an archived project whose display name names a person?

quotes:
Projects imported
under a person's name (R0-79) are renamed by the owner after the import.
An archived project never returns to `active` and cannot be corrected.

| correct a project | owner | the project with the new name, alias (R0-82), customer or object — address, kind, characteristics (R0-45) — next revision of the project | unknown id refused; an archived project refused (R0-12); newly naming a customer that is unknown, erased, restricted or ended refused (R0-16, R0-51, R0-57); a stale revision refused, nothing changes (R0-35) |
judgement.why: The required post-import rename is a project correction, but the texts categorically refuse correction of an archived project.

topics.topic: Meaning and concurrency contract of the session access version
questions: What observable meaning and concurrency behavior does the session access version have?
What changes the access version, and must each owner mutation of session access supply the version it was based on?

judgement.why: This asks the same previously judged question about events that increment the access version and whether it is a concurrency token.

A change states the revision it was made against; a change against an older revision is refused and nothing changes. Every change is atomic.
precedent.why: Mutation preconditions, version-transition rules and stale-input behavior are rules and required tests owned by State 2.

topics.topic: Preservation or replacement of customer references during migration
questions: Must import preserve every legacy `customer_ref`, or must it replace non-Registry identities with newly minted references and rewrite project links through a recorded mapping?
Which customer_ref values are preserved, and how are project links rewritten when a legacy customer_ref is replaced?

quotes:
Import is a one-time, controlled migration of the data the running instances
hold today, through the owner interface and confirmed by the owner. It keeps
every identity and link: project ids, `customer_ref`s, room and pointer ids and
versions.
a v1 `customer_ref` that is not a Registry-minted id becomes a new Customer with a minted `customer_ref`, the old value moving to its tax id when it is one (R0-80)
judgement.why: One passage requires every customer reference identity to be kept, while the other requires some legacy customer references to be replaced with newly minted identities.

topics.topic: Scope of the end-to-end no-personal-data guarantee across services
questions: Is the no-personal-data promise end-to-end across Cabinet and every other service, or only a promise about Registry's direct outputs to Cabinet Kernel?
Is the no-personal-data promise an end-to-end platform guarantee covering Cabinet and other services, or only a guarantee about Registry’s direct outputs to Kernel?

quotes:
It holds no owner credential and no Registry
  service token, never receives a value Registry holds as `personal_data` (R0-26;
  for free text written by others see R0-68), and has no
  administrative access to the production host, its store, configuration,
  secrets or deployment (R0-25).

What other services cleared for
`personal_data` pass on to Kernel is bounded by their own contracts, not here.

Cabinet receives the package of current projects and their context, so its
token allows `personal_data` like those of PresuPro and Client Portal: it lists
projects and reads `context`. What Cabinet passes on to Cabinet Kernel is
bounded by Cabinet's own contract (R0-74).
judgement.divergence: One implementation enforces the promise end to end and forbids Cabinet or any other service from passing Registry personal data through Kernel to the agent; another limits Registry's guarantee to its direct Kernel outputs and permits such forwarding when another service's contract allows it, which the agent, owner and forwarding service notice.
judgement.why: The categorical agent promise and the assignment of other-service forwarding to separate contracts leave the scope of the no-personal-data guarantee open.

topics.topic: Authorized disclosure and deprecation of stored customer ordinary names
questions: May any service read a customer’s ordinary name, and if so through which operation and under what authorization; if not, how do services that previously used it stop keeping a copy?
What is the complete artifact-type vocabulary, and which service owns each type?

topics.topic: Handling an access-request answer that selects an ungrantable project
questions: If the owner answers a pending request by selecting an unknown, archived, anonymised or otherwise ungrantable project, is the answer refused, and does the pending request remain or get cleared?

topics.topic: Owner discovery and navigation of anonymised projects
questions: How can the owner discover and navigate anonymised projects after they disappear from the only project-list action?

topics.topic: Registry values permitted in the Client Portal offline projection
questions: Which exact Registry values may Client Portal’s offline projection retain, and may it contain the customer’s name or other contact data, the project display name, address or object characteristics?

topics.topic: Removal or inspection of personal values in retained anonymised artifact pointers
questions: How can anonymisation guarantee that no personal value remains when retained pointer values are neither inspected nor removed?
